subject: Coffee & Tea
title: First Crack: The Roaster's Signal
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on First Crack: The Roaster's Signal.

hook.text: At around 196°C, coffee beans crack audibly—like popcorn. This is 'first crack,' and it's the roaster's key moment.

buildup.text: Internal steam and CO₂ pressure fracture the bean's cell structure. The crack is an actual physical rupture.

discovery.text: First crack marks the transition from endothermic (absorbing heat) to exothermic (releasing heat). The bean is now self-heating.

twist.text: Most light and medium roasts are pulled during or just after first crack. It's the minimum point for drinkable coffee.

climax.text: A trained roaster judges entire batches by the sound, speed, and uniformity of first crack. It's diagnostic.

punchline.text: Listen for the crack. That sound is where coffee is born.

quiz.question: What causes first crack during roasting?
options: Internal steam and CO₂ pressure fracturing the bean's cell structure

details.summary: First crack is an audible popping sound that signals a critical roasting milestone. Steam and carbon dioxide build up inside the bean until the cell walls fracture. This moment marks the transition from endothermic drying to exothermic flavor development.
details.whyItMatters: First crack tells the roaster the beans are chemically active and flavor is developing rapidly. Most roast profile decisions pivot around this single event.
takeaways: First crack sounds like popcorn popping inside the roaster
It marks the shift from energy absorption to energy release
Light roasts are pulled shortly after first crack begins

faq.question: At what temperature does first crack typically occur in a roaster?
faq.answer: First crack generally happens when the bean temperature reaches around 196 to 205 degrees Celsius (385 to 401 degrees Fahrenheit), though the exact point varies depending on bean density, moisture, and roaster design.

faq.question: What does it mean if first crack is very quiet or absent?
faq.answer: A quiet or absent first crack usually indicates that the beans were dried too slowly or had very low initial moisture, reducing the internal steam pressure needed to fracture cell walls. It often signals a baked roast.
